answer: In an agent marketplace trading timber, violet dye, and yarrow, every agent must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, and each bond can back only one identity at a time. Creating 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million for a month. Splitting funds across wallets cannot increase the number of eligible identities: the attacker must supply fresh capital for every additional seat and forgo its use elsewhere.
